proposals.name: Breitung Township School District Sinking Fund Millage Renewal Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the building and site sinking fund millage that expires with the 2027 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate of 0.8902 mill ($0.8902 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) which may be assessed against all property in Breitung Township School District, Dickinson County, Michigan, be renewed for a period of 10 years, 2028 to 2037, inclusive, to continue to provide for a sinking fund for the acquisition or upgrading of…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the building and site sinking fund millage that expires with the 2027 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate of 0.8902 mill ($0.8902 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) which may be assessed against all property in Breitung Township School District, Dickinson County, Michigan, be renewed for a period of 10 years, 2028 to 2037, inclusive, to continue to provide for a sinking fund for the acquisition or upgrading of technology, for school security improvements, for the construction or repair of school buildings, for the purchase of real estate for sites for school buildings, and all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2028 is approximately $500,382 (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2027 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: BREITUNG TOWNSHIP SCHOOL DISTRICT SINKING FUND MILLAGE RENEWAL PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 0.8902 mills for 10 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.
